transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, yeah, thanks for seeing me. I guess the main reason I’m here is that... well, work is just getting really difficult lately. I manage a few health clinics, and anything that takes real, sitting-down brain work, like doing the monthly reports or planning a multi-site health event... 

Actually, speaking of those, we just tried to do this big blood drive across three counties last month, and the logistics were a total nightmare. The catering company brought the wrong sandwiches, if you can believe it. Tuna salad instead of turkey. Who orders tuna for a blood drive? The smell was just everywhere in the main lobby. My wife actually makes a really great tuna salad, though. She puts little bits of green apple in it, which sounds weird but it gives it this great crunch... 

Wait, sorry, what was I saying? Oh, right. Work. Yeah, so those big planning things or the monthly reports... whenever I have to do them, it just feels like I hit a brick wall. I keep putting them off and putting them off, even when I know it really matters for the staff and the clinics. I just can't seem to make myself sit down and do the heavy thinking.
Did you experience similar problems with attention and organization back when you were in school as a child?

Yeah, actually, I did. Even way back in elementary school. My teachers used to tell my parents that I was, you know, a bright kid, but I was just always daydreaming. Staring out the window. I remember this one classroom in third grade, Mrs. Gable's class, it had these huge windows that looked out over the playground, and past that was this big oak tree. There was this squirrel that lived in it, and I used to watch him bury acorns. He had this whole system going. It's funny how they remember where they put them all, isn't it? Or maybe they don't, maybe they just dig around until they get lucky. I read somewhere that squirrels actually forget a lot of their acorns, and that's how new forests grow. So I guess being forgetful isn't always a bad thing, right? Nature's little tree planters. 

But, uh, yeah, school. I was always losing my worksheets. Just gone. And I'd forget to turn in my homework all the time. The only way anything ever made it to the teacher's desk was if my mother went through my backpack every single night and physically pulled the papers out. Otherwise, it was just a black hole in there.
Do you often feel physically restless, fidgety, or like you're constantly driven by a motor?

No, not really. I don't feel like I have a motor running inside me or anything. 

Actually, speaking of motors, my car has been making this awful rattling noise lately. It's a 2015 Camry, usually super reliable, you know? But every time I hit about 45 miles an hour, it just shudders. I took it to this mechanic down the street from the main clinic, Bob's Auto. Bob is a great guy, he always gives me a discount because we check his blood pressure for him... but anyway, he said it might be the transmission slipping. Which is just great, because transmissions are so expensive. My brother-in-law had to replace his last year and it cost him like three grand. He drives a truck, though, one of those big Ford F-150s. He uses it to haul mulch for his landscaping business. He does really nice work, actually. He planted these beautiful hydrangeas in our front yard, the kind that change color depending on the soil... 

Wait, sorry, what were you asking me? Oh, right, feeling restless. No, physically I'm pretty still. I don't really bounce around or have trouble staying in my chair.
